To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel semi-supervised learning method that dynamically selects the data that provide meaningful and reliable training signals, and hence improves the quality of the back-propagated gradients, leading to better semi-supervised learning.
we propose a novel semi-supervised deep leaning method that exploits the uncertainty information in the training process, which is measured by the variance or entropy under different perturbations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental problem in semi-supervised learning, i.e., how to guide the student model learn more meaningful targets from noisy data.
how to improve the quality of consistency targets and the consistency loss function for semi-supervised learning.
the following questions: (i) How to select data that are most certain or reliable?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a novel semi-supervised learning method by introducing certainty-driven consistency loss to dynamically select data that provide meaningful and certain/reliably targets.
we propose a novel semi-supervised learning method that improves the quality of the targets by filtering out the unreliable data.
we propose to measure uncertainty of predictions under random perturbation, and use it as a criterion to guide the training of the student model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose to dynamically filter data samples with relatively low uncertainty, which can be measured by variance/entropy of predictions under different augmentations and dropout.
we introduce a novel certainty-driven loss to dynamically select certain data for consistency learning.
the proposed method improves the performance of the student model by selecting the data that are relatively certain/reliable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consistency loss should not be minimized for every sample in the training set, as not all training data are equally informative.
we can achieve better performance by focusing on learning from the more certain samples.
not all data samples should be used to minimize consistency loss.
